records.explanation: The rubric itself relies on AC-2-6 s. 4.1.B; no instruction or criterion asks the model to test it. Criterion #6 awards points for stating that DCI2018-10023 was deemed withdrawn on February 13, 2020 under that provision, and penalty #7 deducts 15 points for stating that the case remained active until September 13, 2023. That is what the Order (p.4: 'all while DCI2018-10023 remained an active case') and the Petition report. A model that accurately reads s. 4.1 (Board remands to the Hearing Examiner, deemed withdrawn only for applicant inaction) or follows the record loses credit on both.

No criterion asks the model to check the quotation. The proposition it is cited for (certiorari relief quashes and leaves the matter pending below) is correct law at G.B.V. *844, so the criterion's substance does not reward a wrong rule. The defect is the fabricated quotation and pin cite in grader-facing source text; a model quoting it verbatim would repeat a misquotation.

Criterion #12 (10 points) requires stating that certiorari under s. 163.3215(4) is the exclusive method of challenging a development order. The statute makes certiorari exclusive only where the local government has opted in by ordinance, and otherwise s. 163.3215(3) gives a de novo action that can carry injunctive relief. A model stating the statute accurately may lose the criterion. Penalty #14 (minus 15) penalizes saying petitioners may bring a separate injunction action, a statement s. 163.3215(3) can support for development-order consistency challenges. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

Criterion #13 (10 points) requires stating that s. 163.3167(10) bars invalidation of the project's development order. The subsection reaches only later rulings that land development regulations are invalid for deficient approval standards, and (10)(b) preserves common-law certiorari, so an accurate model would not make the required statement. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

Criteria #16 and #23 name LDC s. 34-83(a)(6) as the Board's remand authority; the quoted language is s. 34-83(a)(4)a.1.b), while (a)(6) is the six-month deemed-withdrawn rule. A grader reading literally may expect the wrong pin cite; the substance (Board may remand to the Hearing Examiner) is supported. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

Criterion #4 (5 points) rewards stating that the Hearing Examiner's recommendation is competent substantial evidence and cites only Hialeah Gardens, which addresses staff testimony and record materials, not hearing examiner recommendations. The criterion rewards relying on the case for a proposition it does not state. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

Criterion #8 (20 points) requires stating that the circuit court erred by finding AC 150/5190-7 (Minimum Standards for Commercial Aeronautical Activities) incorporated into LDC s. 34-1102. The Order never mentions that AC; it relies on land use compatibility and wildlife hazard advisories (AC 150/5190-4B and AC 150/5200-33C as cited in the Petition). The citation is also garbled (5190-7 is dated 2006; Dec. 7, 2023 is AC 150/5190-8). A model that accurately describes the Order cannot make the required statement without misreporting it. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

This appears in criterion #8's source justification: s. 34-1102 is said to incorporate only ACs 150/5300-13B and 150/5200-30D, but it names 150/5200-33B (wildlife attractants), not 30D. The criterion text does not require naming 30D, so the defect reaches grading only through the grader-facing rationale. It understates the section's reference to the wildlife-attractant AC, the AC series the Order relies on. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

Criterion #11 (30 points) requires stating that the circuit court violated separation of powers 'under Fla. Const. art. III, s. 3'. The separation-of-powers clause is art. II, s. 3; art. III, s. 3 governs legislative sessions. A literal grader could withhold credit from a model that cites the correct article. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.
